Shubman Gill has words with umpire after India lose review: 'Height hai, bat nahi hai' 
 Edited by Amit Kumar / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 12:14 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Shubman Gill was unhappy with the decision. (Image credit: X) India captain Shubman Gill was visibly unhappy after India lost a review against Glenn Phillips on the opening day of the first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. The incident took place in the 31st over of New Zealand's innings when JJasprit Bumrah bowled a delivery that moved back towards Glenn Phillips and beat his bat. India appealed for LBW, but the on-field umpire turned it down. Gill discussed the decision with Bumrah before taking the review. Watch Shubman Gill press conference : India's playing XI, bowling combination, Rishabh Pant & more Bumrah felt the ball was too high and told his captain, "height hai" [it's high]. Gill, however, felt Phillips had not edged the ball and said, " bat nahi hai" [no bat]. The Snickometer showed a big spike when the ball passed close to the bat. However, the front-on replay did not clearly show an inside edge. Third umpire Paul Reiffel asked for another replay in slow motion. He felt there was a slight deflection and upheld the on-field umpire Richard Illingworth's not-out decision. Gill was unhappy with the decision. He told Illingworth that there was a gap between the bat and ball and that the delivery had hit Phillips' back pad first. Illingworth explained the decision, but Gill was not convinced. The India captain walked away shaking his head. The delivery also appeared to be going over the stumps. So, even without an inside edge, the LBW decision would most likely have stayed not out. India lost their review. Siraj, Jadeja miss out as India go in with four pacers; Pant returns

 Gill won the toss and elected to bowl against New Zealand. Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja were left out of the playing XI as India opted for a four-pronged pace attack. Gill went with four pacers - Jasprit Bumrah , Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna. Washington Sundar was included as the spin-bowling all-rounder. Rishabh Pant returned to the playing XI after recovering from injury, while Dhruv Jurel also made the cut as the second wicketkeeper-batter. Poll Vote & Share your view
